issues.description: Loop/selection invariant is not stated; `from` detection lacks a literate comment beyond the inline note
issues.detail: The function `findHue` now branches on a positional convention (`args[0] === 'from'`) but never states the invariant: after filtering to word/function nodes, channel N of the color function lives at index N + (isRelativeColor ? 2 : 0), and only when the function is a known hue-bearing form. A two-line comment naming the invariant would let a reader verify correctness without running the tests.

issues.description: `from <color>` is parsed as exactly two tokens, but the origin color may itself be a function with multiple word arguments
issues.detail: The offset of 2 assumes `from` plus a single origin-color token. The test `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` works because `hsl(...)` is one `function` node, but a bare/space-separated origin like `from rgb 1 2 3` or future syntaxes could shift indices. No invariant proves that exactly one node follows `from` before channels begin; an assertion or comment justifying the constant 2 would be appropriate.

issues.description: `0 + offset` is dead arithmetic; write `args[offset]` for the reader
issues.detail: `args[0 + offset]` adds nothing the compiler does not constant-fold and slightly obscures the symmetry with `args[2 + offset]`. Either write `args[offset]` and `args[offset + 2]`, or define `const HUE_INDEX_FIRST = 0, HUE_INDEX_THIRD = 2` and index by name. Small thing; readability is the point.

issues.description: Case folding of `from` is done with `toLowerCase()` per call rather than a single normalized pass
issues.detail: `node.value.toLowerCase()` is already computed; `args[0]?.value.toLowerCase()` duplicates that idiom on a child. Fine asymptotically (constant work), but a single helper `isKeyword(node, 'from')` would be more literate and would centralize the case-insensitivity decision now exercised by the `FROM` test.

issues.description: Test coverage omits the `none` keyword and calc() channels in relative syntax
issues.detail: CSS Color 5 permits `none` and `calc(...)` for any channel, including hue. The added tests cover identifiers (`l c h`) and numbers but not `oklch(from red l c none)` or `oklch(from red l c calc(h + 10))`. Worth a test or two to confirm the rule does not flag or mis-fix these; relative-color edge cases are exactly where false positives hide.

review.summary: The fix is small, local, and correct for the cases tested: detect `from` as the first filtered argument and shift the hue index by 2. Decision: UNDER-AUDITED bordering on RIGOROUS — the algorithm is right but the invariant ("channel N lives at args[N + offset], where offset is 2 iff args[0] is the keyword `from`") is not written down, and the constant 2 silently assumes the origin color is exactly one word/function node. Readability would improve with named indices and a one-line literate comment, and tests should cover `none` and `calc()` channels which are legal in relative color syntax. No correctness defect found under the stated assumptions; complexity remains O(n) in the argument list with trivial constants.
